Recently visited the Hyderabad Cyber Crime Police Station in connection with a client matter where the client’s bank account had been frozen after a cyber-fraud complaint. The issue was related to certain funds received through withdrawals from the Tiranga app. The client had participated in online gaming and, after receiving the withdrawal amount in the bank account, later found that the account had been frozen because the transaction had allegedly become part of a cyber-fraud money trail.

This is not an isolated situation. Many people who have used online gaming platforms have faced similar problems. They receive money from a gaming platform, withdraw it into their bank account, and after some time, the bank account is either frozen or a lien is marked because a transaction somewhere in the chain has been reported in a cyber-fraud complaint. In such cases, the account holder is often left confused about why their own account has been restricted when they have not committed any fraud.

Another common misconception is that if GST has been paid on the gaming transaction, the entire transaction automatically becomes legal. That is not how the law works. GST is a taxation issue, whereas the legality of online money gaming is governed by separate legal provisions. Payment of GST by itself does not provide immunity from an investigation if the transaction is alleged to be connected with an offence.

When I take up such a matter, I do not simply approach the bank and ask them to remove the freeze. The first step is to identify the complaint behind the restriction, examine the disputed transaction, trace the money trail and determine exactly how the client’s account has been connected with the alleged cyber fraud. The bank statement, KYC documents, transaction details, source of funds and the disputed amount are carefully examined before making a representation to the concerned investigating authority.

Under Section 106 of the BNSS, police have powers relating to seizure of property suspected to be connected with an offence, subject to the requirements of law. Therefore, the real question in an account-freeze matter is not merely whether the person received money from a gaming platform. It is whether the particular amount in the account is actually connected with the alleged offence and whether the continued restriction on the account is legally justified.

The objective in such cases is to separate the client’s legitimate funds from the disputed amount, place the complete facts before the investigating authority and seek appropriate relief for removal or modification of the restriction. If the freeze continues without sufficient legal justification, or the entire account is restricted despite a dispute concerning only a specific amount, appropriate legal remedies can be considered before the competent court.
